ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has a schematic of the January and July mean temperatures and precipitation amounts of the two cities A and B. The legend shows that in the “temperature” marker, the hollow circle represents January, and the solid circle represents July. Observing the position of city B, the hollow circle is approximately above 20℃, and the solid circle is approximately around 5℃, indicating that city B has a high temperature in January and a low temperature in July. Reasoning: The seasons in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres are opposite; in the Southern Hemisphere, January is summer and July is winter. City B shows that January is relatively hot and July is relatively cold, which conforms to the seasonal characteristics of the Southern Hemisphere. Therefore, city B is located in the Southern Hemisphere.
